answer: To resist sybils, the protocol requires each reputation slot to anchor a unique proof-of-work chain, like a trellis of verified history, so cloning costs real compute. Agents must stake a bond and pass a random live challenge before each epoch. A would-be attacker must also pay a canyon-wide fee gap: forging N identities demands N bonds plus sustained bandwidth, making the jetty of entry steep. Honest participants earn rebates, while duplicates drain capital, so sybil farming loses money at scale. In practice, Agent0192 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
